chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from his father from Idris ibn Abdillah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two people in ihram who shoot game, and one of them hits it; is the compensation shared between them or on each of them individually? He said: 'On both of them together; each one of them redeems himself separately.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمَيْنِ: Two people in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation ruling when two people in ihram hunt game together?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when two individuals in *ihram* jointly hunt, the compensation (*fidya*) is obligatory on both, with each bearing independent liability for their share. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of individual accountability within joint actions, distinguishing it from shared liability in other contexts. The hadith is situated in the chapter on expiation for unintentional or conditional violations during pilgrimage, emphasizing the precision required in ritual purity and legal obligations.
